fields.description:
*Plan:* Obsidian vault {{Projects/Halo/Implementation Plan.md}}, task T-M1.

*Blocked by:* none.

Labels: {{needs-taylor}}. Blocks T-O3.

*Goal:* I decide how Halo's health data is protected at rest on this PC before real data goes on it, and the decision is recorded on this card.

*Facts:*

* The system drive is {{nvme0n1}} (931.5 GB). The root filesystem {{nvme0n1p2}} is plain ext4 with no LUKS layer. Halo's data would live under {{~/.local/share/halo/}} on that drive.
* The backup drive (T7, {{/media/bear/T7}}) needs no decision: restic encrypts every backup (T-M2).
* The backend only listens on {{127.0.0.1}}, so the risk is a stolen or discarded PC or drive, not the network.

*Options:*

# *Reinstall with full-disk encryption (LUKS).* Strongest. Protects everything on the PC. Costs a backup, reinstall, and restore of the whole machine.
# *Encrypt only Halo's data folder.* A LUKS file container ({{cryptsetup}} on a file, mounted at {{~/.local/share/halo}}) or {{gocryptfs}} mounted there. Small effort. The folder must be unlocked after every boot before {{halo.service}} starts, so the service fails until I unlock it.
# *Accept the risk until the dedicated machine.* No work now. The dedicated machine gets LUKS at install. Data written before then sits unencrypted on this drive; migrating later means copying the folder and then securely erasing the old copy.

* [ ] *Step 1:* Pick an option.
* [ ] *Step 2:* If option 2, set it up and confirm {{~/.local/share/halo}} is the mount point, then add the unlock step to the README "Deploy" section in T-O3's PR. If option 1, do the reinstall before T-O3.
* [ ] *Step 3:* Comment on this card with the option chosen and the date. Move the card to Done.

*Acceptance criteria:*

* The card has a comment naming the chosen option.
